answer: Dynamic entry bonds: each new agent locks a deposit whose price rises with how many identities joined recently, so a sudden gale of sign-ups gets expensive fast while a lone newcomer pays little. The bond stays locked for many epochs and is slashed if graders find the account acting in lockstep with siblings (shared funding source, identical timing). An honest agent tends a slow orchard of rewards that repays its bond; a sybil farm hits a mesa: costs climb steeply, then payouts go flat because clustered accounts are paid as one.
